accessNotes: The supplied modern-author reading links are authorised excerpts, not promises of free complete books. No subscription gate was bypassed.
Concord previews explicitly identify themselves as samples. Links point to the publisher; full copyrighted scripts were not copied into the app.
Miller teacher guides contain selected quotations and commentary, not entire plays. The reading-card notes say this explicitly.
The Paris Review notebook page provides the selected opening entries publicly and then presents a subscription prompt. The entries used precede that prompt.
The modern play dates indicate the original play/first production; Beckett translated-work dates indicate the first English version. Source-edition dates are separately named where known.
exclusions: Generic quote collections, student flashcards, and unattributed social-media quotations were not accepted as final authorities.
Williams’s frequently circulated Camino Real travel aphorism was omitted because the speaker and exact original wording could not be securely verified from an authorised source during this review.
Williams’s We Have Not Long to Love was omitted after the original magazine’s page and ordinary fetch returned access errors.
The inaccessible Theatre Calgary PDF was replaced as evidence by readable Sydney Theatre Company and Mountview materials.
No new Worstward Ho or 1999 Wilson interview excerpts were added, because existing source usage already consumes the available quotation budget.
research.normalization: Preserved wording, capitalization, dialect, and unusual grammar. Curly apostrophe typography and paragraph/line wrapping normalized where needed. Short clause excerpts are identified; they are not silently completed into invented sentences.

specificFindings: All 40 exact text selections match the downloaded primary texts after whitespace collapse only.
All 40 dramatic speakers or narrative voices were checked against surrounding dialogue.
Marius attribution is correct: the preceding chapter introduces the notebook Cosette is about to read, and the following chapter confirms the displayed reflections belong to that notebook.
The Chekhov quotations use Marian Fell consistently for the four plays, including the Fell spellings of character names. The Lady with the Dog uses Constance Garnett.
Ibsen Wild Duck and Lady from the Sea use Eleanor Marx Aveling; Hedda Gabler and Master Builder use Gosse and Archer; Ghosts uses Archer. No mixed translation wording found.
Hedda Gabler’s 1907 copyright note is consistent with the edition label; the source explicitly mentions reproduction from 1914 and 1926 printings.

The first-series Chekhov translator credit and 1912 date are corroborated in the introduction to Gutenberg 7986; its Cherry Orchard reading link is Julius West, not the earlier Calderon translation mentioned by West.
Swan Song 1887, revised Ivanov 1889, and Uncle Vanya 1897 intentionally distinguish original publication/revision from later production dates and old chronology errors.
Tartuffe reading link explicitly carries Jeffrey D. Hoeper’s public-domain grant. All twelve reading URLs returned HTTP 200 and include complete Gutenberg texts.
No source works newly excerpted here were found in the existing five baseline data files; audit exclusions are consistent with direct source search.
No material quotation, speaker, locator, or translation-name defects found.

findings.finding: The context attributes the observation that their bodies still change to Clov. In the Grove excerpt, Hamm makes this observation, and Clov then points out the contradiction. The quoted line and Hamm speaker attribution are correct.
findings.suggestedReplacement: Hamm claims that nature has abandoned them, then observes that their bodies still change. Clov points out the contradiction, making the exchange a dark joke about aging rather than a literal claim about nature.
